page: Microsoft Azure M96bds_2_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the MBDSMediumMemoryv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8473C processor operating at 4.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 1946.0 GB of RAM, translating to 20.27 GB of memory per core, alongside 4608 GB of local storage. The x86_64 architecture supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier performance across memory and computational workloads. The server achieved top-tier status in memory bandwidth tests, recording 7459.57 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 429.2 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Multi-core processing capabilities are strong, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 91198.3 and a Passmark CPU score of 97234.14. Cryptographic and database operations also perform in the top tier, as evidenced by a Passmark database operations score of 35122.57 and a Redis SET throughput of 114.97 million operations per second.

This server is designed for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, large-scale relational databases, in-memory analytics, and heavy data-processing pipelines. The high resource density of 1946.0 GB RAM combined with 4608 GB of local storage provides a balanced profile for hosting massive databases without relying solely on external network storage. The presence of AMX instructions also enables efficient CPU-based machine learning inference, as demonstrated by strong performance in medium-sized LLM prompt processing and text generation.
